raw.assessment: The incumbent delivers a removable, assembled partition set and includes an order check and layout diagram. These provide plausible opportunities to catch selection and placement errors, but their effectiveness is unmeasured. Reported component errors and unpacking confusion indicate distinct possible failures; neither establishes their cause. O6 limits an account of uniformly slow assembly: both workers achieved seven to nine minutes on repeated three-compartment orders, whereas mixed batches contained every extreme delay. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. O5 also weakens a width-only explanation for insertion retries because measured widths overlap. The combined timing cannot identify the dominant delay. Current evidence does not demonstrate any pilot success threshold.

openings.claim: Repeated changes between order layouts may increase selection and checking work, contributing to mixed-batch delays and component errors.
openings.delta: Tests whether order switching contributes beyond the inherent work of larger layouts.
openings.prediction: For the same layouts and worker, mixed sequences increase selection/checking time or discrepancies relative to grouped sequences, without a comparable increase in insertion time.
openings.probe: Reuse six spare sample organizers across grouped and mixed sequences containing identical layout counts; reverse sequence order between workers. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and audit components against each order. Treat practice and reuse effects as limitations. Stop the probe before it threatens accepted-order delivery.
assumptions: Sample trials fit available working time and the initial spending cap.
Reusable sample cycles approximate production sufficiently for an exploratory comparison.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement with the existing removable parts.
openings.delta: Tests layout interpretation after independently verifying component completeness.
openings.prediction: Verified complete kits with the tailored diagram produce fewer short-partition placement questions than equivalent kits with the current diagram.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants, five per diagram, using the same ordered layout and verified parts. Record unaided completion and short-partition questions within ten minutes. This is an exploratory discriminator, not proof of 90% success. Check printing cost and preparation time before production use.
assumptions: Diagram preparation fits the fixed delivery date and 500 initial/0.40 recurring cost limits.
Instructions alone can resolve at least some observed placement confusion.

raw.assessment: The observations leave open whether some demand for corrective work and customer assistance is generated by parts organization and layout guidance. Neither mechanism is established; small probes cannot certify the 60-order success targets.

openings.claim: Shared shape bins during mixed-layout assembly may generate switching and corrective-picking demand. Corrective returns to those bins could increase interference for the other worker, sustaining that demand.
openings.delta: Test order-specific staged component sets while retaining full assembly, selected counts, and exterior colors.
openings.prediction: With layout mix held constant, staged sets should reduce corrective picks and selection/checking time. A reduction confined to assembly time that is offset by staging time would not support a workshop-time benefit.
openings.probe: Use existing templates and reusable sample parts for matched mixed-layout sequences under shared-bin and staged-set conditions; reverse condition order across workers. Log staging, selection, insertion, checking, packing, corrective picks, and final component accuracy. Include staging in total time and compare identical layouts.
assumptions: Sample work fits spare capacity before the fixed delivery date.
Staging uses existing bench space and materials; any added expense must stay within both cost caps.
Corrective returns and worker interference are unobserved hypotheses.

openings.claim: Showing three possible layouts may generate uncertainty about the ordered arrangement, prompting unnecessary rearrangement and apparent-shortage reports that create workshop replacement demand.
openings.delta: Make the ordered layout and its component inventory primary on the existing insert, retaining rearrangement guidance.
openings.prediction: For independently verified complete kits, order-specific guidance should reduce short-partition questions and false shortage reports while improving unaided arrangement success. Unchanged confusion would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Assign the ten participants to two groups balanced by layout difficulty, using ten sample organizers: current versus order-specific guidance. Independently audit contents before unpacking; record unaided success, short-partition placement, questions, and shortage reports. Treat results as directional and record insert preparation time and cost.
assumptions: Actual missing components remain possible and require separate correction.
The revised insert preserves footprint, capacity, removable partitions, accepted selections, delivery date, and both cost caps.

openings.claim: Switching may increase selection/checking delays/errors beyond complexity.
openings.discriminator: Identical layouts fare worse in mixed versus grouped sequences.
openings.probe: Reuse six samples; reverse sequences across workers; time selection/insertion/checking/packing separately; audit contents.

openings.claim: Shared-bin corrective picking may sustain worker interference; staging may reduce it.
openings.discriminator: Fewer corrective picks and lower total time including staging.
openings.probe: Match mixed layouts across shared-bin/staged conditions; reverse across workers; log staging, four production steps, corrective picks, accuracy.
openings.uncertainty: Interference/returns unobserved; staging may transfer work.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout guidance locating short partitions and listing inventory may reduce confusion, unnecessary rearrangement and false-shortage replacement demand.
openings.discriminator: Complete kits yield fewer placement questions/false shortages and more unaided success.
openings.probe: Randomize ten participants, five/diagram, using ten verified kits of identical layout; record ten-minute success, placement, questions, shortages, preparation time/cost; retain rearrangement guidance.
openings.uncertainty: Actual omissions remain possible; shortage reports establish no cause.

post_distill.decision: Exploratory only; synthetic observations and small probes prove no pilot threshold. Preserve 30x20 footprint, assortment, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors; enforce 500 initial/0.40 recurring caps, available bench/workers/samples. Stop before delivery risk. Width overlap weakens width-only explanation.
